author: Paul, who calls himself "a prisoner of Jesus Christ," writing with Timothy (1:1). He signs part of it in his own hand (1:19).
recipients: Philemon, a believer and fellow-worker of Paul, with Apphia, Archippus, and the church that met in Philemon's house (1:1-2).

date.traditional: About AD 60-62, during Paul's imprisonment in Rome, at the same time as Colossians.
date.scholarly: Nearly all scholars accept that Paul wrote it. Some place his imprisonment at Ephesus (about AD 54-55) or Caesarea (about AD 57-59) instead of Rome.

writtenFrom: Prison (1:1, 1:9-10). The letter does not name the city; Rome is the traditional view.
destination: Colossae, a town in the Lycus valley of the province of Asia. The letter does not name it, but Colossians names Onesimus as "one of you" and sends a message to Archippus (Colossians 4:9, 4:17).
purpose: To appeal to Philemon to receive back Onesimus, his servant, who had left him and had become a believer through Paul, "not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved" (1:10-16). Paul offers to repay any debt himself (1:18-19).
setting: Slavery was part of ordinary household life in the Roman world. Onesimus had been "unprofitable" to Philemon and had "departed" (1:11, 1:15). He travelled back with Tychicus, who also carried Colossians (Colossians 4:7-9).

outline.title: Thanksgiving for Philemon's love and faith

themes: Paul appeals for love's sake rather than commanding (1:8-9).
In Christ a servant becomes "a brother beloved" (1:16).
Paul takes another's debt on himself (1:18-19).
Faith shows itself in love toward all the saints (1:5-7).
basis: From the letter's own text, compared with Colossians; dating views summarized from standard introductions.
